title: Derivative-consistent adaptive retention interpolant
question: Can a shared smooth retention interpolant provide both theta(h) and C(h)=dtheta/dh consistently, while K is represented separately, so that Richards retains its analytical convergence path without losing the runtime advantage of tabulated hydraulics?

representation.knot_slopes: derived from authoritative analytical C through dz/dx
representation.theta_runtime: reconstruct Se from z, then theta
representation.capacity_runtime: differentiate the same Hermite interpolant and apply the chain rule to obtain dtheta/dh
representation.conductivity_runtime: separate log(K) lookup on the same knot support
representation.near_saturation: authoritative exact handling for h > -1 cm

stage_1.runtime_rule: candidate must be faster than full analytical theta+C+K for all tested materials

stage_2.required_convergence: same nonlinear iteration and backtracking counts as analytical

scientific_rationale: F-AHL07 showed that independently approximating C while theta is exact changes the Newton path, consistent with Jacobian/residual inconsistency. F-AHL08 showed that keeping theta and C fully analytical and looking up only K has no useful speed benefit. The next candidate therefore approximates theta and C together as one derivative-consistent object.
